text:
pager: INCIDENT: elevated tail latency (p90/p99) on hosted inference in us-west-2; streaming response subsystem showing backlog and 503 spikes. Auto-created incident channel: #inc-3050001234

sre_maya: saw it at 12:04 UTC, tail spiking ~5x. Errors concentrated on streaming endpoints /v1/stream and websocket handshakes.

ara: paging oncall now, joining. any customer-facing impact data yet? :eyes:

devon: frontend alerts: increased reconnects from clients using SSE and websockets, some customers reporting truncated responses. No new deploys in last 30m.

eng_ryan: looking at host metrics — some inference nodes hitting cpu/gpu throttles, but backlog mostly in the push delivery tier (mux layer) fanning out to many clients. suspect a fanout amplification with large open streams.

product_sam: we need quick mitigation that reduces load without full rollback. Can we switch streaming to short-poll fallback for a window?

ops_leila: suggestion: enable response-mode=short-poll on edge for hosted tenants for 15 minutes while we stabilize. This toggles server-push off and returns poll-friendly responses. Low risk config flip.

eng_ryan: agree. Two parts: 1) edge toggle to disable server-initiated frames (handshake eviction), 2) tighten per-connection rate quotas so abusive clients back off. I'll prepare commands.

deploy_bot: deploy approved by rotation: @ara. Rolling config change to edge-config cluster-edge-1 in us-west-2. ETA ~2m.

ara: i'm on the toggle, will cut server-push in us-west-2 and set short-poll ttl=10s. Notifying status page and support.

ara: (after) done. edge config flipped: server_push.enabled=false, client_poll.ttl=10s. Also set connection_quota=20/min for unauthenticated.

devon: metrics starting to flatten — p90 latency down ~30% in last 90s, error rate falling. reconnects still a bit high but stabilizing. :thumbsup:

eng_ryan: rerouted remaining streaming traffic to canary worker pool with reduced concurrency to avoid cascading. Also applied temporary KV-cache policy to reduce repeated decode cost.

sre_maya: starting customer impact assessment: small number of high-throughput customers experienced partial degraded UX (responses now polled instead of streamed). No data loss. Logging contactable customers.

product_sam: draft message for customers: "We temporarily switched streaming to poll mode to stabilize latency; you'll see slightly delayed chunking but full responses preserved. We're monitoring and will restore streaming once stable." Send to priority customers?

ops_leila: done — sent to top 10 paying customers and support templated note to all active sessions.

eng_ryan: plan for next 30m: monitor latency, error budget, and connection churn. If stable for 10m, progressively re-enable server_push on a canary subset (10% traffic) with health checks. If any regression, rollback to poll.

ara: creating follow-up task: INCIDENT-3050001234 -> postmortem + recommended throttling defaults to prevent fanout amplification.

devon: @sre_maya can you handle paging handoff? i'm taking shift for stabilization ops for the next 45m.

sre_maya: received, taking the on-call baton at 12:18 UTC. I'll coordinate the rollback test when we hit stabilization criteria.

eng_ryan: added temporary rate-limiter rule to global route: 
```
route: /v1/stream
rule: if conn_open_time < 60s then max_frames_per_minute=30
```
This will reduce burst frame emission.

deploy_bot: config change applied to edge clusters us-west-2-a/b.

devon: any idea root cause?

eng_ryan: preliminary hypothesis: certain SDK clients open many idle streams with keepalive activity causing mux to fan out and decode repeated prefix tokens. Need to add client-side guidance and server heuristics.

product_sam: add guidance to SDK docs about connection pooling and prefer fewer multiplexed conversations. Also consider a server-side idle eviction policy.

ara: I'll keep the incident open until we restore streaming and run a 24h post-incident check. For now status: MITIGATED (polling mode active, latency improved).

sre_maya: logging timeline and handoff notes, will page if any backslide. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
